findings.problem: Two of the four citation hazards the review acceptance requires to be tested are neither caught nor declared out of the lane's scope: an arm cited by POSITION and a basename-only path both pass with exit 0 and 0 citations checked, and no surface (checker usage/RULE block, run record policy, acceptance artefact) names either class — a zero-hit grep for basename|abbreviat|position-?only|ordinal|cited by position|cannot see|not checkable|blind. A reader cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'not in the family', which contradicts the lane's own principle that silence is not acceptable.
findings.requiredFix: Add one named boundary clause to the checker's usage/RULE block AND to every run record's policy block, in the lane's own vocabulary: an arm cited by POSITION (no literal) and an abbreviated path (a basename with no `/`) are OUT OF FAMILY and pass silently, because the citation family's six addressing parameters require a repo-relative literal.

findings.problem: `--naive` is advertised as a mode in the lane's record (T80.mode) and read in driverHeadersMain, but the rows are built with `driverRow(file)` without passing `naive`, so `--driver-headers --naive` and `--driver-headers` produce identical readings and differ only in the record's `mode` label (measured on both revisions: R11 == R12, R13 == R14).
findings.requiredFix: Either wire the flag (pass `{ naive }` to the row builder, keeping the audit's precise baseline separate) or drop `[--naive]` from the advertised usage and from the record's mode vocabulary.

findings.problem: The record stores `revisions.durable_checker.lines = 1143` for the artefact its own `after` hash pins (fbdc0256…), which measures 1146 (`wc -l` and `awk END{NR}` agree; the file ends with a newline). A recorded reading that does not reproduce against the artefact it describes.
findings.requiredFix: Re-measure and correct the count (or drop it: the hash is the identity, the count is decoration that rots).
